data.name: Help.ITEMS.Purpose
data.value: This page lists the items (materials kept in stock: active ingredients, excipients, packaging, intermediates) with their identity, material type and stock behaviour. Each item is created here and taken through its statuses: “Draft”, “Awaiting approval”, “Active”, “Deactivated”, “Retired”.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step1
data.value: Narrow the list with the search box, or click “Filter”, choose “Status” or “Material type” and click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step2
data.value: Click “Add item”, fill in the identity and the stock behaviour on its full-page form, then click “Save”: the item is saved as “Draft”. In a single-line field of that form, Enter saves it too (in the “Description” box Enter starts a new line). Later, on an active item only the name and the description change freely; a filled stock field needs an approved correction.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step3
data.value: Open a draft's “Actions” and choose “Send for approval”: the item stays “Awaiting approval” until it is approved, and only then becomes “Active”. While it is awaiting approval, the person who sent the request can choose “Withdraw Approval Request” in its “Actions”: the item goes back to its previous status.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step4
data.value: “Deactivate” takes an active item out of new stock entries; “Request reactivation” goes through the same approval again; “Retire” is final, is allowed only for a deactivated item with zero stock, and the code is never reused. Each of them asks for a reason.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step5
data.value: Outside a text field, with no dialog or side panel open, the “?” key opens this help with the page's shortcuts.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Purpose
data.value: See how much of each product you hold, by warehouse, location, lot and stock status. The list is read-only: stock changes only through movements.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Audience
data.value: Warehouse staff, stock controllers, purchasing and production planners

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Step1
data.value: If the page asks, choose the company in “Company”. Then click the filter icon (“Filter”), pick “Product”, “SKU”, “Warehouse”, “Location”, “Lot number” or “Stock status” and click “Apply”; “Reset” clears the filters.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Step1Title
data.value: Narrow the list

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Step2
data.value: Filter by a product or SKU and the cards above the list show “Total on hand”, “Available”, “Quality inspection” and “Quarantine / blocked” for that selection. Without a product filter the cards stay empty on purpose.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Step2Title
data.value: Read the totals

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Step3
data.value: Each row is one product at one place, lot and status. “On hand” is what is physically there, “Reserved” is already set aside, and “Available” is what you can still use.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Step3Title
data.value: Read a stock row

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Step4
data.value: In a row’s actions, “History” opens the movement history filtered to that product and lot; “Movement” opens a new movement with this row already set as the source.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Step4Title
data.value: Trace or move a row

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Step5
data.value: To add stock (an opening balance or a count gain), click “New stock entry”. The “Movement history” tab shows every movement behind the balance.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGER.Step5Title
data.value: Book incoming stock

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Purpose
data.value: Book stock that arrives outside a document flow: an opening balance or a count gain. The stock list is never edited directly; this page posts an inbound movement.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Audience
data.value: Stock controllers, warehouse supervisors

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Immediate
data.value: “Post movement” books the stock at once, with no confirmation. A posted movement cannot be edited; a mistake is fixed in the movement history with “Reverse” or “Correct”.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Step1
data.value: In “Movement type”, choose “Opening balance” or “Count gain”. The type decides which target fields appear below.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the entry type

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Step2
data.value: Select the “Product” first, then its “SKU”; only that product’s SKUs are listed.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Step2Title
data.value: Pick product and SKU

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Step3
data.value: Fill “Target warehouse”, “Target location” and “Target stock status”, and choose the “Lot” when the SKU is lot-tracked.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Step3Title
data.value: Say where it goes

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Step4
data.value: Enter “Quantity” and “Unit” (and the serial numbers if the SKU asks for them), then “Document no.”, “Transaction date” and “Posting date”.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Step4Title
data.value: Enter quantity and dates

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Step5
data.value: Check the before and after figures in “Stock effect”, then click “Post movement”. “Cancel” returns to the stock list without posting anything.

data.name: Help.STOCKLEDGERCREATE.Step5Title
data.value: Check and post

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Purpose
data.value: Every stock movement of the company, newest first. Movements are never edited: a mistake is cancelled with a reversal and, if needed, replaced by a new movement.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Audience
data.value: Stock controllers, warehouse supervisors, auditors

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Step1
data.value: If the page asks, choose the company in “Company”. Click the filter icon (“Filter”), set “Product”, “Lot number”, “Warehouse”, “Location”, “From date” or “To date” and click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Step1Title
data.value: Narrow the history

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Step2
data.value: Each row shows the “Transaction no.”, “Movement type”, product and quantities, where the stock went, and “Recorded by”: the person who posted it.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Step2Title
data.value: Read a movement

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Step3
data.value: On a manual movement, “Reverse” opens a confirmation; “Reverse movement” posts an opposite movement that cancels it. The original row stays in the history.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Step3Title
data.value: Reverse a movement

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Step4
data.value: “Correct” opens the correction page with the movement’s values filled in. It posts a reversal plus the corrected movement, so both records stay visible.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Step4Title
data.value: Correct a movement

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Step5
data.value: Click “New movement” for a count loss, scrap, write-off or transfer. The “Stock list” tab shows the balance these movements produce.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTS.Step5Title
data.value: Post a new movement

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Purpose
data.value: Post a manual stock movement: an opening balance, a count gain or loss, scrap, a write-off, a transfer or a customer return. Every movement is kept for good and changes stock the moment it is posted.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Audience
data.value: Stock controllers, warehouse staff

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Immediate
data.value: “Post movement” changes stock at once, with no confirmation. A posted movement cannot be edited; a mistake is fixed in the movement history with “Reverse” or “Correct”.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Step1
data.value: Start with “Movement type”. The type decides whether you need a source, a target or both, and the form shows only those fields.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the movement type

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Step2
data.value: Select the “Product” first, then its “SKU”; only that product’s SKUs are listed.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Step2Title
data.value: Pick product and SKU

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Step3
data.value: For outgoing stock and transfers, choose the stock row in “Source (lot / location)”. For incoming stock and transfers, fill “Target warehouse”, “Target location” and, where asked, “Target stock status” and “Lot”.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Step3Title
data.value: Set source and target

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Step4
data.value: Enter “Quantity” and “Unit” (and the serial numbers if the SKU asks for them), then “Document no.”, “Transaction date” and “Posting date”.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Step4Title
data.value: Enter quantity and dates

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Step5
data.value: Check the before and after figures in “Stock effect”, then click “Post movement”; the receipt opens. “Cancel” returns to the movement history without posting.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTCREATE.Step5Title
data.value: Check and post

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Purpose
data.value: Fix a manual movement that was posted wrongly. The original is never changed: this page posts a reversal that cancels it and then the corrected movement, so both stay in the history.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Audience
data.value: Stock controllers, warehouse supervisors

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Step1
data.value: The “Movement being corrected” card shows the original’s “Transaction no.”, “Movement type”, product, quantity and lot.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Step1Title
data.value: Check what you correct

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Step2
data.value: The form opens with the original values. Change what was wrong, for example “Quantity”, “Target location” or “Lot”, and check the dates.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Step2Title
data.value: Fix the values

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Step3
data.value: Look at the before and after figures in “Stock effect” before you post.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Step3Title
data.value: Check the stock effect

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Step4
data.value: Click “Correct”. A confirmation explains the two records; “Reverse and post” posts the reversal and the corrected movement, then the receipt opens.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Step4Title
data.value: Confirm the correction

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Step5
data.value: If the reversal went through but the corrected movement was refused, a warning stays on the page. Fix the field it names and click “Post corrected movement”; nothing is posted twice.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTEDIT.Step5Title
data.value: Finish a partial correction

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Purpose
data.value: The receipt of the movement you have just posted: what was booked, where the stock went and the balance it left. It is shown once, right after posting.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Audience
data.value: Stock controllers, warehouse staff

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Step1
data.value: The green banner gives the number of the posted movement. After a correction, a second banner names the reversal and the corrected movement.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Step1Title
data.value: Check the result

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Step2
data.value: The cards repeat what you entered: “Movement type”, “Product”, “SKU”, “From”, “To”, “Lot”, “Quantity”, “Document no.” and the dates.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Step2Title
data.value: Review the movement

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Step3

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Step3Title
data.value: See who recorded it

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Step4

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Step4Title
data.value: Read the new balance

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Step5
data.value: Click “Movement history” to return to the list of movements, or “Stock list” after a stock entry.

data.name: Help.STOCKMOVEMENTDETAILS.Step5Title
data.value: Go back

data.value: Find locations

data.name: Help.LOCATIONS.Step2

data.value: Status, history and stock

data.name: Help.LOTS.Purpose
data.value: See every lot of the company's products in one list: its dates, its status and how much of it is on hand. From here you open a lot, change its status or start a new one.

data.name: Help.LOTS.Audience
data.value: Warehouse, quality and planning staff

data.name: Help.LOTS.Step1
data.value: Type a lot number or a manufacturer / supplier lot in the search box, or click the filter icon, choose “Product”, “Status”, “Expiry before” or “Only lots with a warning” and click “Apply”. “Clear” empties the filters.

data.name: Help.LOTS.Step1Title
data.value: Narrow the list

data.name: Help.LOTS.Step2
data.value: The “Status” column shows Draft, Released, Blocked or Expired; “Expiry” warns when the date is near or past, and “On hand” is the lot's stock in the selected company.

data.name: Help.LOTS.Step2Title
data.value: Read status and expiry

data.name: Help.LOTS.Step3
data.value: Click a row or “Lot detail” to see the whole lot. The row menu also offers “Edit”, “Movement history” and “Traceability”.

data.name: Help.LOTS.Step3Title
data.value: Open a lot

data.name: Help.LOTS.Step4
data.value: Choose “Change status” in the row menu, pick the new status and write a reason of at least 10 characters. Blocking makes all stock of the lot unusable, so you must tick “I understand the impact.” first. Expired is set by the system only.

data.name: Help.LOTS.Step4Title
data.value: Change the status

data.name: Help.LOTS.Step5
data.value: Click “New lot” to register a lot by hand; it is saved as Draft.

data.name: Help.LOTS.Step5Title
data.value: Add a lot

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Purpose
data.value: Everything about one lot on one page: its status and warnings, stock on hand, where the stock is, its serial numbers and who changed what and why.

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Audience
data.value: Warehouse, quality and planning staff

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Step1
data.value: The status badge and warnings sit next to the lot number. “Stock on hand” shows the quantity, “Lot information” the dates, origin and source of the lot.

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Step1Title
data.value: Check the lot

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Step2
data.value: “Stock distribution” lists each “Warehouse”, “Location”, “Stock status” and “Quantity” of this lot in the selected company.

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Step2Title
data.value: See where the stock is

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Step3
data.value: “Change history” shows who changed which field, old → new, and the reason. Use ‹ and › to page through it; records cannot be deleted.

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Step3Title
data.value: Read the history

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Step4
data.value: Click “Edit” to correct the lot's fields, or “Change status” to release or block it with a reason of at least 10 characters.

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Step4Title
data.value: Edit or change status

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Step5
data.value: Open “Movement history”, “Traceability” or “Open in Stock Ledger” at the top; for a serial-tracked lot, “All serials” in “Serial numbers” opens the Serial Explorer.

data.name: Help.LOTDETAILS.Step5Title
data.value: Go further

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Purpose
data.value: Register a lot by hand for a lot-tracked product, with its dates and origin. The new lot is saved as Draft.

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Audience
data.value: Warehouse and quality staff

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Step1
data.value: Pick the “Product”, then the “SKU” the lot belongs to. Only lot-tracked products can get a lot.

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the product

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Step2
data.value: Type the “Lot No”: 1–40 characters, A–Z, 0–9 and . / -. It cannot be changed after saving, and must be unique for the product.

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Step2Title
data.value: Enter the lot number

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Step3
data.value: Enter the “Manufacturing date”, “Expiry date” and, if needed, “Retest date”: manufacturing is today or earlier, expiry comes after manufacturing, retest lies between them.

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Step3Title
data.value: Fill in the dates

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Step4
data.value: Optionally fill in “Manufacturer lot”, “Supplier lot”, “Country of origin” and “CoA reference”.

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Step4Title
data.value: Add the origin

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Step5
data.value: Check the “Summary” card and click “Save”. “Cancel” returns to the Lot Explorer without saving.

data.name: Help.LOTCREATE.Step5Title
data.value: Save

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Purpose
data.value: Correct the details of an existing lot: dates, origin and references. Every change is kept in the lot's change history.

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Audience
data.value: Warehouse and quality staff

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Step1
data.value: “Product”, “SKU” and “Lot No” cannot be changed after the lot is saved; they are shown read-only.

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Step1Title
data.value: Know what is fixed

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Step2
data.value: If the lot is not a draft, the fields stay locked until you write at least 10 characters in “Reason for the change”. The reason is kept in the change history.

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Step2Title
data.value: Write a reason

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Step3
data.value: Correct the “Manufacturing date”, “Expiry date”, “Retest date”, “Manufacturer lot”, “Supplier lot”, “Country of origin” or “CoA reference”.

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Step3Title
data.value: Change the fields

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Step4
data.value: “Changes to be saved” lists every field you changed, old → new, before you save.

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Step4Title
data.value: Check the changes

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Step5
data.value: Click “Save”. “Cancel” returns to the lot detail without saving.

data.name: Help.LOTEDIT.Step5Title
data.value: Save

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Purpose
data.value: See every Stock Ledger movement of one lot: what came in, what went out, where it went and in which stock status.

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Audience
data.value: Warehouse, quality and planning staff

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Step1
data.value: Search for and pick the lot in the “Lot” selector above the table. When you come from a lot, it is already selected.

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the lot

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Step2
data.value: Click the filter icon, set “From date” and “To date”, then click “Apply”. “Reset” removes the dates.

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Step2Title
data.value: Limit the dates

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Step3
data.value: Each row shows the “Transaction no”, “Movement type”, “Quantity” (+ in green for incoming, − in red for outgoing), “To”, “Status”, “Source” and “Transaction date”.

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Step3Title
data.value: Read the movements

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Step4
data.value: Click a row or “Movement receipt” to see the movement as the ledger recorded it; “Open in Stock Ledger” takes you to the ledger.

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Step4Title
data.value: Open the receipt

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Step5
data.value: When you arrive from the Serial Explorer, a “Serial …” chip names the serial and its last movement is highlighted in the list.

data.name: Help.LOTMOVEMENTS.Step5Title
data.value: Follow a serial

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Purpose
data.value: Find any serial number: where it is now, which lot it belongs to and whether it can be used. This page is read-only.

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Audience
data.value: Warehouse, quality and service staff

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Step1
data.value: Type the serial number in the search box above the list.

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Step1Title
data.value: Find a serial

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Step2
data.value: Click the filter icon, choose “Product”, then “Lot” and “Status” (Active, Blocked, Consumed), and click “Apply”. “Reset” clears the filters.

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Step2Title
data.value: Narrow the list

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Step3
data.value: “Warehouse / location” shows where the serial is, “Last movement” when it last moved, and “Status” whether it can be used; a serial is Blocked when its lot is blocked.

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Step3Title
data.value: Read where it is

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Step4
data.value: Choose “Lot detail” in the row menu to open the lot the serial belongs to.

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Step4Title
data.value: Open its lot

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Step5
data.value: Choose “Movement history” in the row menu: the lot's movements open with this serial's last movement highlighted.

data.name: Help.SERIALS.Step5Title
data.value: See its movements

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Purpose
data.value: Follow a lot backwards to where it came from and forwards to where it went, two levels each way, and see how much quantity is affected.

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Audience
data.value: Quality, recall and warehouse staff

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Step1
data.value: Search for and pick the lot in the “Lot” selector. When you come from a lot, it is already selected.

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the lot

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Step2
data.value: “Total affected quantity” adds on hand and shipped per unit (units are never added together); the cards show “In stock”, “Shipped” and “Affected lots”.

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Step2Title
data.value: See the affected quantity

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Step3
data.value: “Selected lot” is in the centre, with “Backward · level 1–2” on one side and “Forward · level 1–2” on the other. For now backward shows the lot's receipt source and forward shows outbound document numbers only.

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Step3Title
data.value: Read the flow

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Step4
data.value: Click a lot card to put it in the centre and trace from there; “Lot detail” on the selected lot opens its full page.

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Step4Title
data.value: Move through the chain

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Step5
data.value: If you may run recalls, “Full trace (recall)” opens the recall trace for this lot.

data.name: Help.LOTTRACE.Step5Title
data.value: Start a full trace

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Purpose
data.value: Link the lot texts that were typed by hand into old Stock Ledger movements, before lots were registered, to registered lots. The migration does not change past movements; it only adds the lot link.

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Audience
data.value: Inventory and quality managers

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Step1
data.value: The cards show “Total rows”, “Matched” and “Pending”. Use the “All”, “Pending” and “Matched” tabs to see only the rows you need; each row is one product + “Typed lot”.

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Step1Title
data.value: See what is left

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Step2
data.value: Where “Suggested match” shows a lot, choose “Apply suggestion” in the row menu, or click “Apply all suggestions” to take every suggestion at once.

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Step2Title
data.value: Take the suggestions

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Step3
data.value: Choose “Link to existing lot” to pick a registered lot of the same SKU, or “Typo — link to another lot” to join the row to another typed lot, then click “Link”.

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Step3Title
data.value: Link by hand

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Step4
data.value: Choose “Create as new lot”, check the lot number and dates, and click “Use as decision”. The lot is created as Draft only when you confirm the migration.

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Step4Title
data.value: Create a lot

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Step5
data.value: Decisions stay on this page until you confirm; “Change” reopens a row. When nothing is pending, click “Confirm migration” and write a reason of at least 10 characters. This cannot be undone: afterwards, typing a lot by hand in the Stock Ledger is closed.

data.name: Help.LOTMIGRATION.Step5Title
data.value: Confirm the migration

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Purpose
data.value: Follow every stock line waiting in quarantine for a quality decision: see what is overdue, put stock on hold by hand and open each record to decide.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Audience
data.value: Quality assurance and warehouse leads

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Step1
data.value: Select your “Company”. The cards show the lines awaiting a decision, the total quantity per unit and the records past the waiting target; overdue rows are highlighted in the list.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the company

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Step2
data.value: Type in the search box or click the filter button (“Filter”), choose a warehouse, stock status, source or “Overdue only”, then click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Step2Title
data.value: Narrow the list

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Step3
data.value: Click “Quarantine stock”, pick the lot, its available row and the quantity, click “Continue” and confirm with a reason of at least 10 characters. The record then waits in this queue.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Step3Title
data.value: Put stock on hold by hand

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Step4
data.value: Click a row or “Details” to see the record’s quality information, decision history and stock movements.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Step4Title
data.value: Open a record

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Step5
data.value: Click “Decide” on an open record to release, reject or block it. The stock moves only after the decision is approved.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEQUEUE.Step5Title
data.value: Decide

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Purpose
data.value: See everything about one quarantine record — lot, quantity, quality information, decision history and stock movements — and move it towards a decision.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Audience
data.value: Quality assurance and warehouse leads

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Immediate
data.value: Saving the analysis note

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Step1
data.value: Check the facts at the top, the “Quality information” card and the stock movements the record made; a yellow band warns when the waiting target is exceeded.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Step1Title
data.value: Read the record

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Step2
data.value: Click “Start review” to move the record to In review. No stock moves.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Step2Title
data.value: Start the review

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Step3
data.value: Click “Edit note”, write the analysis result and click “Save”. The note is locked while a decision is awaiting approval.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Step3Title
data.value: Write the analysis note

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Step4
data.value: Click “Decide” to open the decision page and release, reject or block the stock.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Step4Title
data.value: Decide

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Step5
data.value: In the Workflow box use “Refresh status”, “Sign and send” for a draft, “Withdraw decision” or “Re-apply” when a decision could not be applied. Signatures appear in “Decision history”.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDETAILS.Step5Title
data.value: Follow the approval

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Purpose
data.value: Make the quality decision for a quarantine record — release, reject or block — sign it and send it for approval. Nothing moves until it is approved.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Audience
data.value: Quality assurance decision makers

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Step1
data.value: Choose “Release”, “Reject” or “Block”. To split the quantity, turn on “Partial decision” and give two lines with different decisions whose total equals the record’s quantity.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the decision

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Step2
data.value: For reject or block pick a “Block reason”. For a release tick “CoA / analysis result checked”; a lot past its retest date also needs a “New retest date”.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Step2Title
data.value: Complete the details

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Step3
data.value: Write a “Reason” of at least 10 characters. The note at the top tells you whether the four-eyes rule makes another QA user approve.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Step3Title
data.value: Write the reason

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Step4
data.value: Click “Next: Electronic signature”. A draft is created (no stock moves) and “Decision to be signed” shows it; use “Back” to change it.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Step4Title
data.value: Go to the signature step

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Step5
data.value: Click “Sign and send” and sign in the e-signature window (or “Send for approval” when the policy asks no signature). The stock moves after the approver approves.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINEDECIDE.Step5Title
data.value: Sign and send

data.name: Help.DECISIONSUBMIT.Purpose
data.value: Sign and send a draft decision that was not created on a form here — for example a lot release request or a decision whose sending failed. The stock moves after approval.

data.name: Help.DECISIONSUBMIT.Audience
data.value: Quality assurance decision makers

data.name: Help.DECISIONSUBMIT.Step1
data.value: Read “Decision to be signed”: the lines and their target status, the planned stock movement and the reason, as the server built them.

data.name: Help.DECISIONSUBMIT.Step1Title
data.value: Check the decision

data.name: Help.DECISIONSUBMIT.Step2
data.value: Click “Sign and send” and sign in the e-signature window (or “Send for approval” when the policy asks no signature). The decision then awaits approval.

data.name: Help.DECISIONSUBMIT.Step2Title
data.value: Sign and send

data.name: Help.DECISIONSUBMIT.Step3
data.value: Click “Cancel” to return to the queue; nothing is sent.

data.name: Help.DECISIONSUBMIT.Step3Title
data.value: Leave without sending

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Purpose
data.value: Manage the stock that is blocked: block more stock right away, finish the review, and decide what happens to it — a disposition or an unblock.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Audience
data.value: Quality assurance and warehouse leads

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Immediate
data.value: “Block stock” → “Block”: the chosen stock becomes Blocked at once, without an approval workflow

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Step1
data.value: Type in the search box or click the filter button (“Filter”), choose a block reason, “Awaiting disposition only” or a “Status”, then click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Step1Title
data.value: Narrow the list

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Step2
data.value: Click “Block stock”, pick the lot, its available row, the quantity and a “Block reason”, write a reason of at least 10 characters and click “Block”.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Step2Title
data.value: Block stock

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Step3
data.value: When the investigation is finished, click “Complete review” on the row and give a reason. This opens the unblock option.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Step3Title
data.value: Complete the review

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Step4
data.value: Click “Disposition decision” to destroy, return to the supplier, rework or keep the stock as a sample.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Step4Title
data.value: Decide the disposition

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Step5
data.value: Click “Unblock” on a reviewed record and give a reason. The decision is signed and sent for approval; the stock becomes Available only after approval.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDSTOCK.Step5Title
data.value: Unblock

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDDISPOSITION.Purpose
data.value: Decide what happens to a blocked stock record — destroy, return to the supplier, rework or keep as a sample — and send the decision for signature and approval.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDDISPOSITION.Audience
data.value: Quality assurance decision makers

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDDISPOSITION.Step1
data.value: Choose “Destroy”, “Return to supplier”, “Rework” or “Retain as sample / reference”; each card shows the stock movement it creates.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDDISPOSITION.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the disposition

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDDISPOSITION.Step2
data.value: Enter the “Quantity” (at most the blocked quantity; the rest stays Blocked). A return needs a “Supplier” and the “Return document no.”; destruction needs a “Destruction method” and “Destruction date”. A sample needs a sample location set in Quarantine settings.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDDISPOSITION.Step2Title
data.value: Enter the quantity and details

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDDISPOSITION.Step3
data.value: Write a “Reason” of at least 10 characters and check the box “Movement the stock ledger gets on approval”.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDDISPOSITION.Step3Title
data.value: Write the reason

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDDISPOSITION.Step4
data.value: Click “Next: Electronic signature”, check the summary, then click “Sign and send” (or “Send for approval”). The stock moves after approval.

data.name: Help.BLOCKEDDISPOSITION.Step4Title
data.value: Sign and send

data.name: Help.RETESTQUEUE.Purpose
data.value: See the lots whose retest date has passed or is coming soon, and send them to quarantine for a quality decision.

data.name: Help.RETESTQUEUE.Audience
data.value: Quality assurance and warehouse leads

data.name: Help.RETESTQUEUE.Step1
data.value: The list shows lots past their retest date or due within 30 days, with a status: upcoming, past due and closed to use, or already in quarantine. A lot past its date cannot be sold, reserved or issued until a quality decision is made.

data.name: Help.RETESTQUEUE.Step1Title
data.value: Read the list

data.name: Help.RETESTQUEUE.Step2
data.value: Type a product or lot in the search box to narrow the list.

data.name: Help.RETESTQUEUE.Step2Title
data.value: Find a lot

data.name: Help.RETESTQUEUE.Step3
data.value: Click “Quarantine” on the row and confirm with a reason of at least 10 characters. The lot’s available stock moves to Quarantine and a record is added to the quarantine queue.

data.name: Help.RETESTQUEUE.Step3Title
data.value: Quarantine the lot

data.name: Help.RETESTQUEUE.Step4
data.value: For a lot already in quarantine, click “Open the quarantine record” to follow its decision.

data.name: Help.RETESTQUEUE.Step4Title
data.value: Open the existing record

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Purpose
data.value: Set your company’s quarantine rules: the waiting target, four-eyes and lot release approval, who may approve, where samples are kept and which block reasons exist.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Audience
data.value: Quality managers and administrators

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Immediate
data.value: “Save” for the settings and saving a block reason take effect at once

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Step1
data.value: Enter the “Waiting target (days)” (1–60) and the “Re-read interval (seconds)”, and turn “Four eyes” and “Lot release approval” on or off.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Step1Title
data.value: Set the general rules

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Step2
data.value: Under “Approver candidates” choose a position or a user and click “Add” (at most 10). Without a candidate no decision can be sent for approval.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Step2Title
data.value: Choose the approvers

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Step3
data.value: Under “Sample locations” choose a warehouse and its sample location, then click “Add”; one location per warehouse.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Step3Title
data.value: Set the sample locations

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Step4
data.value: Click “Save” at the top. If the approval template shows as missing, click “Prepare the approval template” once.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Step4Title
data.value: Save and prepare the template

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Step5
data.value: Click “Add block reason”, enter a code and a name in all seven languages, then save; use the row action to edit an existing one.

data.name: Help.QUARANTINESETTINGS.Step5Title
data.value: Manage block reasons

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Purpose
data.value: See your company's expiry risk at a glance: expired stock still on hand, critical and approaching lots, receipts below the minimum remaining shelf life, open exceptions and FEFO compliance.

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Audience
data.value: Quality assurance, warehouse managers and supply planners

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Step1
data.value: Pick your company in “Company” if you are asked, then narrow the figures with “All warehouses” and the “Period” of the compliance card; the page refreshes as soon as you change them.

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the scope

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Step2
data.value: The expired, critical and approaching cards count lots and quantities against your company's thresholds shown in the subtitle; the exception card tells you how many cases are past the SLA.

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Step2Title
data.value: Read the cards

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Step3
data.value: Click the “Expired stock” card or the critical or approaching card to open the matching list, already filtered by your warehouse.

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Step3Title
data.value: Open the lots behind a card

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Step4
data.value: The chart shows month by month how much “Available” and “Held” stock will expire.

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Step4Title
data.value: Look ahead 12 months

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Step5
data.value: In “Top 10 risk lots” use the row icons “View FEFO order”, “Quarantine (MOD-0175)” (opens the Quarantine module) or “Open exception”; “See all” opens the full approaching list.

data.name: Help.EXPIRYDASHBOARD.Step5Title
data.value: Act on the riskiest lots

data.name: Help.EXPIRYAPPROACHING.Purpose
data.value: List the lots that expire soon, earliest expiry first (FEFO order), with available and held stock in separate columns, so you can use or handle them in time.

data.name: Help.EXPIRYAPPROACHING.Audience

data.name: Help.ESIGNAUDITEXPORT.Step3Title
data.value: Download the file

data.name: Help.ESIGNAUDITEXPORT.Step4
data.value: The “Export audit log” lists every export with its number, date, person, format, record count, filter and file digest.

data.name: Help.ESIGNAUDITEXPORT.Step4Title
data.value: Check the log

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Purpose
data.value: Keep the signature sample you can use when you sign electronically, and follow the history of your samples. You have one active sample at a time, and saving a new one always asks for your password.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Audience
data.value: Everyone who signs electronically

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Immediate
data.value: Deactivating and deleting a sample; without the approval rule, a saved sample becomes active at once

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Step1
data.value: “My signature sample” shows your active sample, when it was added, who approved it and how many signatures used it; click the image to enlarge it.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Step1Title
data.value: See your sample

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Step2
data.value: Under “New signature sample” draw on the “Draw” tab (set “Thickness” and “Color”, or use “Full screen (landscape)” on a phone), or on the “Upload image” tab choose a PNG or JPG of up to 1 MB, crop it and, if needed, turn on “Clear the background”.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Step2Title
data.value: Draw or upload

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Step3
data.value: Click “Save with password”, enter your “Password” and click “Verify and save”.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Step3Title
data.value: Save with your password

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Step4
data.value: If the policy requires approval, the new sample shows “Waiting for approval” until another e-signature administrator approves it; until then your current sample stays in use. You can never approve your own sample.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Step4Title
data.value: Wait for approval

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Step5
data.value: In “Signature sample history” use “Deactivate” on the active sample or “Delete” on a sample that was never used; a sample used in a signature cannot be deleted, only deactivated.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMYSIGNATURE.Step5Title
data.value: Manage old samples

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Purpose
data.value: Decide which actions require an electronic signature, with which meaning and visual signature rule, and how often the password is asked. Changes apply to new signatures; each one needs a reason and is written to the change history.

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Audience
data.value: e-Signature administrators

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Immediate
data.value: Saving the policy and reverting a company to the tenant default; both apply to new signatures at once

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Step1
data.value: Click “Tenant default” for the policy every company without its own uses, or “Per company” and pick the company.

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the scope

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Step2
data.value: If the company uses the tenant default, click “Separate policy for this company” to start from a copy; rows that differ are tagged “Different”. “Revert to the tenant default” removes the company policy after you give a reason.

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Step2Title
data.value: Give a company its own policy

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Step3
data.value: In “Signature rules per action” set each action to “Required” or “Off” and choose its “Signature meaning” and “Visual signature”; “Second factor” is “Coming soon”.

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Step3Title
data.value: Set the rules per action

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Step4
data.value: Under “General settings” choose “Ask for the password at every signature” or “Once within a time window” and set the “Validity of the password re-check” (1–60 min). “Require administrator approval before a signature sample is used” is a tenant-wide setting.

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Step4Title
data.value: Set the password rule

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Step5
data.value: Click “Save with a reason”, write a reason of at least 10 characters and click “Save”; the change appears in the “Change history”. Without the right to manage the policy, the page is read-only.

data.name: Help.ESIGNPOLICY.Step5Title
data.value: Save with a reason

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Purpose
data.value: Define what a signature declares, for example I approve or I reviewed; the signing window offers the active meanings. Once a meaning is used its code is locked, and every signature keeps the meaning text of the moment it was signed.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Audience
data.value: e-Signature administrators

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Immediate
data.value: Saving, activating and deactivating a meaning

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Step1
data.value: Click “Filter”, choose “Status” or “Usage” and click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Step1Title
data.value: Find a meaning

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Step2
data.value: Click “New meaning”, enter the “Code” (2–32 characters starting with a capital letter: A–Z, 0–9, _), the “Display name” in all 7 languages and, if you like, a “Description”, then click “Save”.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Step2Title
data.value: Add a meaning

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Step3
data.value: Click “Edit” on a row; a used meaning keeps its code, and a name change affects new signatures only. Without the right to manage meanings the row offers “View”.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Step3Title
data.value: Edit a meaning

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Step4
data.value: Use the switch in the “Status” column and confirm with “Activate” or “Deactivate”. A deactivated meaning cannot be chosen for new signatures, and a meaning used by a policy row cannot be deactivated.

data.name: Help.ESIGNMEANINGS.Step4Title
data.value: Activate or deactivate

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Purpose
data.value: Review the new signature samples waiting for approval when the policy requires it. An approved sample becomes its owner's only active sample, and every decision is kept permanently in the decision history.

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Audience
data.value: e-Signature administrators

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Immediate
data.value: Approving and rejecting a sample

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Step1
data.value: Click “Filter”, choose “How it was added” and click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Step1Title
data.value: Narrow the queue

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Step2
data.value: Click the image in the “Image” column to enlarge it with its owner, date and digest.

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Step2Title
data.value: Check the image

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Step3
data.value: Click “Approve” and confirm with “Approve”; the user's previous active sample becomes inactive.

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Step3Title
data.value: Approve

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Step4
data.value: Click “Reject”, write a “Reason” of at least 10 characters and confirm with “Reject”; the user sees the reason on the My Signature page.

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Step4Title
data.value: Reject

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Step5
data.value: For your own sample the row shows “Another administrator decides” instead of the buttons. Every decision appears in the “Decision history” below.

data.name: Help.ESIGNSAMPLEAPPROVALS.Step5Title
data.value: Leave your own sample

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Purpose
data.value: Set the evidence a rep must give when starting a visit: location, photo, institution QR code and device verification. The setting is layered and the most specific wins: a business unit setting overrides the legal entity setting, which overrides the tenant setting; a time-boxed exception relaxes a rule for one rep for a while.

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Audience
data.value: Sales operations managers

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Immediate
data.value: Saving and applying the setting

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step1
data.value: On the “Scoped settings” tab, pick the tenant, a legal entity or a business unit in “Scopes”. For a new scope click “Add legal entity” or “Add business unit”; it starts empty and every field comes from above.

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the scope

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step2
data.value: In the “Setting form”, click “Change in this scope” on a field you want to change; “Back to the setting above” takes it from above again. Click “Save”, check the changed rows and how many reps it reaches, and confirm with “Save and apply”.

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step2Title
data.value: Change the fields and apply

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step3
data.value: “See a rep's effective setting” shows each field's value and the scope it comes from. “Change history” shows who changed what and when, filtered by scope; “Reps” shows the scope applied to each rep. “Remove the scope” returns its reps to the setting above at once; confirm with Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac).

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step3Title
data.value: Follow the source and the history

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step4
data.value: On the “Time-boxed exceptions” tab, click “New exception”. Enter the rep, the rules to relax, a date range of at most 30 days and the reason, then click “Send for approval” or press Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac).

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step4Title
data.value: Request a time-boxed exception

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step5
data.value: The exception is approved in the Task Center; the requester cannot approve their own. Only an approved exception within its dates applies. In the quick view, “Cancel exception” and “End early” ask for a reason; type it and confirm with Ctrl+Enter.

data.name: Help.VISITEVIDENCESETTINGS.Step5Title
data.value: Manage the exception

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Purpose
data.value: Review the evidence flags of started visits: a far or missing location, a short visit, a QR code not scanned or invalid, a start under an exception. A flag is a hint to look into; on its own it does not mean a rule was broken.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Audience
data.value: Area managers and the sales operations team

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step1
data.value: For “Period”, choose “Last 7 days”, “Last 30 days” or “Custom range…”. A custom range can be at most 92 days.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the period

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step2
data.value: Filter by “Rep”, “Institution” and flag type. “Flagged only” is on; turn it off to list visits without flags too.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step2Title
data.value: Narrow the list

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step3
data.value: The cards on top show “Visits started”, “Flagged visits” and “By flag type”. One visit can carry several flags.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step3Title
data.value: Read the summary

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step4
data.value: The row's quick view shows the location, the distance to the institution, the QR code result and any exception; seeing the photo needs its own permission. “Open the visit” opens the visit itself.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step4Title
data.value: Open the evidence

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step5
data.value: The “Rep summary” tab shows started and flagged visits per rep, the rate and the most frequent flag. Clicking a row filters the visit list to that rep.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITEVIDENCEFLAGS.Step5Title
data.value: Compare the reps

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Purpose
data.value: See the e-mails the CRM sent automatically from visit reports — report summary, adverse event, off-label request, report overdue — with their recipients and status, and open each one as it was written. No e-mail address is shown.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Audience
data.value: Representatives (their own visits), line managers (their team) and the sales operations team

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Step1
data.value: Set the “Period”: the last 30 days, the last 7 days, this month or a “Custom range…”. The period is the day of the visit.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the period

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Step2
data.value: Filter by “E-mail type”, “Status” and — as a manager — “Representative”. “PV route pending” means the PV safety e-mail is not set and only the line manager was informed.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Step2Title
data.value: Narrow the list

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Step3
data.value: The “Recipient” column shows roles, never addresses: “Line manager”, “PV safety”, “MSL”. A safety e-mail goes to PV or MSL with the line manager in copy.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Step3Title
data.value: Read the recipients

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Step4
data.value: The row's “Quick view” shows the e-mail as it was sent: the subject, “To”, “Cc”, “Date”, the content and “View report”.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Step4Title
data.value: Open the e-mail

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Step5
data.value: With the settings permission, the “Notification settings” tab sets the “PV safety e-mail” and the “MSL e-mail” and switches the report summary and the overdue reminder. If someone saved meanwhile, reload and save again.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITNOTIFICATIONS.Step5Title
data.value: Set the mailboxes

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Purpose
data.value: Manage the QR codes posted at the institutions' reception desks. The rep scans this code when starting a visit; a sub-unit without its own code uses its parent institution's code.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Audience
data.value: The sales operations team

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Immediate
data.value: Generating, regenerating and revoking a code

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step1
data.value: Filter the list by “Region”, “City”, “Institution type” and “QR status”. “Last scan” and “Last 30 days” show whether the code is in use.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step1Title
data.value: Find the institutions

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step2
data.value: Select rows and run “Generate for selected (those without a code)”; institutions that already have an active code are skipped. Up to 200 institutions can be selected at a time.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step2Title
data.value: Generate codes in bulk

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step3
data.value: Print one code with the row's “Print the code” and several with “Print selected (label sheet)”. On the print page, choose “Single” or “Label sheet” and click “Print”.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step3Title
data.value: Print

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step4
data.value: On the institution's page, use “Regenerate” or “Revoke” on the “Institution QR code” card. Both make the posted and printed old codes invalid at once; revoking asks for a reason.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step4Title
data.value: Renew or revoke a code

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step5
data.value: Whether the code is required or optional is the “Institution QR code” setting on the Visit Evidence page. Under the required setting, a visit started at an institution without a code is flagged.

data.name: Help.CRMVISITQRCODES.Step5Title
data.value: Read it with the setting

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Purpose
data.value: Set the limits that class a doctor's monthly patient count in a product's indications as Low, Medium or High. A product row comes before the tenant default; when neither exists, the built-in values apply.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Audience
data.value: Sales operations and marketing managers

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Immediate
data.value: A threshold change

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step1
data.value: On the “Thresholds” tab, the “Tenant default” row stays on top in every sort order; product rows take precedence over it. The “Source” column shows where a value comes from.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step1Title
data.value: Read the thresholds

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step2
data.value: The row's “Edit” action opens the side panel. Enter “Low below (X)” and “High above (Y)”; try a monthly patient count in the preview to see its class.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step2Title
data.value: Edit

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step3
data.value: Click “Save” or press Enter; check the changed values and confirm with “Yes, save”. The change takes effect at once.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step3Title
data.value: Save

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step4
data.value: For a product that needs limits different from the default, open its own row with “Add product”.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step4Title
data.value: Add a product

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step5
data.value: The “Change history” tab shows every change with the person, the row and the old → new value; the list can be exported as CSV or Excel.

data.name: Help.CRMDOCTORINSIGHTTHRESHOLDS.Step5Title
data.value: Follow the history

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Purpose
data.value: Write approved answers to the objections a rep may hear from a doctor during a visit. An approved answer is chosen as an expected objection in knowledge path steps and appears in the rep's notes during the presentation.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Audience
data.value: Content teams and medical approvers

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Immediate
data.value: Retiring an answer

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step1
data.value: Narrow the list by “Product”, “Category” and “Status”, or search the objection text.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step1Title
data.value: Filter the library

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step2
data.value: Click “New objection response”; fill in “Product”, “Category”, “Objection · the doctor’s question” and “Approved answer”, choose supporting claims from the product's approved claims and click “Save draft”.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step2Title
data.value: Write an answer

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step3
data.value: “Send for approval” locks the answer during review; “Withdraw” returns it to draft.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step3Title
data.value: Send for approval

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step4
data.value: The approver chooses “Approve”, or writes a note and chooses “Return to draft”. The person who wrote or sent the answer cannot approve it.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step4Title
data.value: Approve or return

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step5
data.value: An approved answer cannot be changed; open a new draft with “New draft from copy”. “Retire” drops the answer from every presentation at once and cannot be undone; “Where it is used” shows which steps are affected.

data.name: Help.OBJECTIONRESPONSES.Step5Title
data.value: Change or retire

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Purpose
data.value: Manage the products reps choose as competitors in their reports: company, active ingredient, the products of ours they compete with, and price and reimbursement per country.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Audience
data.value: Master data and sales operations teams

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Immediate
data.value: Saving, deactivating

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step1
data.value: Filter by “Our product”, “Company”, “Active ingredient”, “Country” or “Status”; the search also covers other names.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step1Title
data.value: Filter the list

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step2
data.value: Click “New competitor product”; enter the name, company, active ingredient and at least one of our products, write the box price and reimbursement on the country rows and click “Save”. “Rep view” shows the card the rep will see in the report.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step2Title
data.value: Add a record

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step3
data.value: On the “Rep proposals” tab, new competitors written by reps in their reports are waiting. With “Decision”, prepare a complete, merge or reject decision and click “Send for approval”.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step3Title
data.value: Decide on proposals

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step4
data.value: The decision applies once it is approved in the Task Center; whoever prepared it cannot approve it. Until then, the proposal is used only in the proposing rep's reports.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step4Title
data.value: Wait for approval

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step5
data.value: The details page shows “Usage in reports” and “Change history”. “Merge with another record” links the record to another one after approval and cannot be undone; “Deactivate” makes it unselectable in new reports.

data.name: Help.COMPETITORPRODUCTS.Step5Title
data.value: Manage a record

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Purpose
data.value: Plan, visit and report your week in one calendar. When you start a visit, the evidence the tenant asks for (location, photo, institution QR code) is taken; the report is sent within 48 hours.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Audience
data.value: Field reps and area managers

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Immediate
data.value: Approving the week, starting a visit, sending a report

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step1
data.value: Switch to “Plan” mode; drag target doctors onto a day or a time. Add products to an institution's planned doctors with “Apply products”.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step1Title
data.value: Plan the week

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step2
data.value: When the plan is ready, click “Approve the week”. An approved week is read-only; to change it, use “Reopen the week” with a reason.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step2Title
data.value: Approve the week

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step3
data.value: In “Execute” mode, open today's visit and click “Start visit” when you arrive at the institution. Depending on the setting, a photo, the location and the “Institution QR code” are asked for; then “Start presentation” opens the presentation.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step3Title
data.value: Start the visit

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step4
data.value: After the visit, click “Send the report”. You have 48 hours for the report; after that the record is locked.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step4Title
data.value: Report

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step5
data.value: For a visit that did not take place, choose “Not done” or “Reschedule” and give the reason. You can add an unplanned visit for today with “Unplanned visit”.

data.name: Help.VISITWORKSPACE.Step5Title
data.value: Close what did not happen

data.name: Help.PREORDERS.Purpose
data.value: Lists the pharmacy pre-orders you may see — your own, your team's and those waiting for your approval — with their status and the depot's answer.

data.name: Help.PREORDERS.Audience
data.value: Representatives, their managers (approvers) and sales operations.

data.name: Help.PREORDERS.Step1Title
data.value: Filter the list

data.name: Help.PREORDERS.Step1
data.value: Open “Filter”: period, status, pharmacy, depot, product, country — an approver also has “Awaiting my approval”.

data.name: Help.PREORDERS.Step2Title
data.value: Read the amounts

data.name: Help.PREORDERS.Step2
data.value: Each total carries its own currency; orders in different currencies are never added up. “Local equivalent” can be shown from Column Visibility.

data.name: Help.PREORDERS.Step3Title
data.value: Open the quick view

data.name: Help.PREORDERS.Step3
data.value: The eye icon shows the lines, the totals and the timeline, with links to the document and the approval.

data.name: Help.PREORDERS.Step4Title
data.value: Record the depot's answer

data.name: Help.PREORDERS.Step4
data.value: Sales operations marks a sent order “Delivered” or “Partially delivered” (boxes per line and a note) in the quick view.

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERFORM.Purpose
data.value: Takes a pharmacy's order to be passed to its depot; the depot issues the invoice. The company, the currency and the prices come from the system.

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERFORM.Audience
data.value: Field representatives (tablet and phone).

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERFORM.Step1Title
data.value: Choose the pharmacy and the products

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERFORM.Step1
data.value: Search the pharmacy, then add products with their quantity, MF (for example 10+2) and — when a price list is in force — the discount.

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERFORM.Step2Title
data.value: Watch the rule badges

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERFORM.Step2
data.value: Each line says “Within limits”, “Approval needed” or “Not allowed”, with the limit it passed. A line that is not allowed must be corrected.

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERFORM.Step3Title
data.value: Save and let the pharmacist sign

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERFORM.Step3
data.value: “Save draft” gives the order number. Choose the depot, then hand the device to the pharmacist for the signature. A change of lines clears the signature.

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERFORM.Step4Title
data.value: Send

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERFORM.Step4
data.value: “Send” opens when nothing blocks it (the reasons are written under it); it reads “Send for manager approval” when an approval is needed. The sent order opens on its details page: it waits for the approver or, when the tenant allows it, goes straight to the depot.

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERAPPROVE.Purpose
data.value: Decides a pre-order that waits for you: approve it, reject it or send it back for changes.

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERAPPROVE.Audience
data.value: The representative's manager (the Reports-to position).

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERAPPROVE.Step1Title
data.value: See why it is with you

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERAPPROVE.Step1
data.value: “Why is it with me?” names the tenant setting or the lines over a soft limit.

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERAPPROVE.Step2Title
data.value: Compare with the limits

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERAPPROVE.Step2
data.value: Each cell shows what was entered and, under it, the rule's limit; the pharmacy's last six months are on the right.

data.name: Help.COMPREORDERAPPROVE.Step3Title
